answer: Name: Concurrent divergent challenge test. The scheduler sends each identity two overlapping challenges seeded by independent public beacons. One beacon is read at a basalt ridge station. Another is read at a knoll sensor. A third is read at a jetty tide gauge. Each challenge requires a fresh signed state transition. A shared clone cannot answer both from one state without forking, so batch reuse fails. To pass, an attacker must allocate one dedicated mutable state, execution slot, and separate challenge log per identity, paying that runtime plus storage and latency for each.
